No passive tutorial marathons

The four-session learning loop

Each concept should move through recall, observation, failure, and application. That turns recognition into usable knowledge.

Understand

Read one focused explanation. Close it and explain the concept in your own words, including the problem it solves.

Predict

Read a small code sample and predict its output, execution order, allocations, or failure before running it.

Break and debug

Introduce or repair a realistic defect. Use breakpoints, logs, tests, and documentation before asking AI for the answer.

Apply and recall

Run or modify one small disposable example, then return later and reproduce the explanation without notes.

Checkbox rule

When can I mark something complete?

  1. I can explain it without notes.
  2. I can identify it in unfamiliar code.
  3. I can write or modify a small example.
  4. I know a common failure or misuse.
  5. I know when not to use it.

What completion means

Knowledge supports senior work; it does not award seniority.

Course mastery demonstrates technical breadth. Senior-level evidence also requires repeated production decisions, ownership through failures, clear trade-offs, safe delivery, and raising the effectiveness of other developers.

Your AI contract

Think first. Ask second. Verify always.

Before AI: write your understanding, proposed flow, edge cases, and first attempt.

With AI: request questions, hints, review, competing designs, or missing cases.

After AI: explain the answer unaided, test it, and reject anything you cannot debug.

Reusable tutor prompt

Teach me this as a backend code-review exercise. Do not give me the solution first. Ask me to predict the behaviour, challenge incomplete reasoning, and give one hint at a time. End by making me explain the concept and one misuse without notes.
